description: A task queue with a worker harness and a small page

commits.message: chore: set up the project and local postgres

steps.title: Add the queue store
steps.body:
Postgres tables and the store on top of them.

`claim` is one statement using `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so concurrent claims pass over each other's rows. Dedupe rests on a primary key, so two enqueues racing on one key give one task. Backoff is a pure function, tested on its own.

commits.message: feat: add the schema and the connection
feat: add exponential backoff with jitter
feat: claim, ack, nack and recover tasks in the store

steps.title: Expose the queue over HTTP
steps.body:
The eight endpoints from the brief, plus `GET /queues` for the page, `PUT /queues/:name` for per-queue settings and `GET /tasks/:id` to read a result.

Inputs are validated with zod, and every error answers `{ error: { code, message } }`. Tests run against real Postgres.

commits.message: feat: add the http api and its server
test: cover the api against real postgres

steps.title: Add the worker harness
steps.body: A library a worker process imports: `register` a handler per type, then `start`. It claims in batches, routes by type, acks or nacks, and heartbeats at half the lease. An unknown type fails the task rather than dropping it.

commits.message: feat: add the worker harness with heartbeats
test: cover routing, retries and lease renewal

steps.title: Add the llm, js and http handlers
steps.body: Each decides what is worth retrying: a `503` is, a `SyntaxError` is not. The `js` handler runs scripts in a child process under Node's permission model, so a crash or a hang there cannot touch the worker. The `llm` handler sits behind `LlmProvider`, with a stub for now.

commits.message: feat: run js scripts in an isolated child process
feat: add the llm handler behind a provider interface
test: cover what each handler retries

steps.title: Test claims under concurrency
steps.body: 50 mixed tasks and 4 workers against real Postgres: every task is processed and none is held by two workers. A second test fires 10 claims at the same instant.

steps.title: Add the queue page
steps.body: One HTML file with no build step: each queue's counts, refreshed every 2 seconds, and a drill-in to its DLQ with a requeue per row.

steps.title: Document how to run it and why it works
steps.body: The README covers running it and what is left out. DESIGN.md covers the claim, the lease model, a dead worker state by state, retries and idempotency.

commits.message: ci: run the tests against postgres

issues.title: Claim must be safe when workers compete
issues.body: Ten workers calling `claim` at once must never hold the same task. Needs a test against real Postgres, not a mock.

issues.title: Recover tasks from workers that die
issues.body: A worker that dies holding a task must not leave it stuck. Use leases, and renew them while a long handler runs.

issues.title: Decide what each task type retries
issues.body: A `503` should retry and a `SyntaxError` should not. Write down where the line sits for `llm`, `js` and `http`.

issues.title: Show queues and their DLQ on a page
issues.body: Ready, in-flight and DLQ counts that refresh on their own, and a requeue action per DLQ row.

issues.title: Clean up finished tasks and old dedupe rows
issues.body: Both tables grow without bound today. Add a retention job, with the retention period set per queue.

DESIGN.md.old: - **`js`** runs in a child process under Node's permission model and a fresh `vm` context: no files, no child processes, no `require`, and a 10 second timeout. A crash or a hang takes down only the child.
DESIGN.md.new: - **`js`** runs in the worker's own process with `new Function`, which keeps it fast and lets scripts use Node's APIs.
